channels.name: SDA
channels.direction_master: bidirectional — Push-Pull (data, post-Sr header) + Open-Drain (S, arbitrable header, ACK, DAA, IBI arbitration)
channels.direction_slave: bidirectional — Open-Drain (ACK, IBI / Hot-Join arbitration, DAA PID/BCR/DCR output) + Push-Pull (Slave-Read data + T-Bit)
channels.purpose: Serial Data Line. Carries the 9-bit Address Header (7-bit address + RnW + ACK) and the 9-bit SDR Data Word (8 data + T-Bit). Drive mode switches dynamically during the same transaction. Optional High-Keeper weakly maintains HIGH between active drivers.
channels.active_levels: Push-Pull mode: 0 / 1 actively driven. Open-Drain mode: 0 = LOW (driven by any device); 1 = HIGH-Z (pulled up by Rp / High-Keeper).

channels.name: SCL
channels.direction_master: output — Push-Pull normally; Open-Drain only in legacy / arbitration windows
channels.direction_slave: input — Slaves shall NOT drive SCL (clock-stretching is forbidden on I3C)
channels.purpose: Serial Clock Line. Master generates all clock pulses; 9 SCL pulses per word (Address Header or SDR Data Word). Master may stall SCL LOW under specific transitory conditions per Table 11.
channels.active_levels: Push-Pull 0/1 normally; Open-Drain only in I3C Legacy / I2C mode

global_signals.name: VDD
global_signals.purpose: Supply voltage (1.2 V / 1.8 V / 3.3 V typ). Logic thresholds: VIL ≤ 0.3 VDD, VIH ≥ 0.7 VDD.

global_signals.name: Rp / Pull-Up
global_signals.purpose: Pull-Up resistor on SDA (and possibly SCL in legacy mode) to VDD; sized per Cb ≤ 50 pF and target rise time tCR.

global_signals.name: High-Keeper
global_signals.purpose: Optional weak Pull-Up on SDA that maintains HIGH between active Push-Pull drivers (during turnaround windows).

global_signals.name: GND
global_signals.purpose: Common ground reference for all devices on the bus.

handshake_pairs.name: ADDR_HDR_ACK
handshake_pairs.rule: After 8-bit address+RnW: Slave drives SDA LOW Open-Drain on 9th SCL pulse → ACK; HIGH → NACK.

handshake_pairs.name: BROADCAST_ACK
handshake_pairs.rule: After 7'h7E + W: every I3C Slave that is in scope ACKs collectively (wired-AND); at least one Slave must drive LOW.

handshake_pairs.name: WRITE_T_BIT_PARITY
handshake_pairs.rule: After each Master-Write data byte: Master drives T-Bit = XOR(Data[7:0],1) Push-Pull; Slave NACKs at next byte on mismatch (error S2).

handshake_pairs.name: READ_T_BIT_EOD
handshake_pairs.rule: After each Slave-Read data byte: Slave drives T-Bit = 1 (continue, releases SDA HIGH-Z next clock for Master abort window) or T-Bit = 0 (end-of-message).

handshake_pairs.name: IBI_ARBITRATION
handshake_pairs.rule: From Bus Available, Slave drives its Dynamic Address (RnW=1) Open-Drain; lowest address wins; Master ACK/NACK on 9th pulse.

handshake_pairs.name: HOTJOIN_ARBITRATION
handshake_pairs.rule: From Bus Idle, Slave drives Hot-Join Address 7'h02 (RnW=0); Master ACK/NACK; ACK + ENTDAA triggers DAA.

handshake_pairs.name: DAA_PID_ARBITRATION
handshake_pairs.rule: During ENTDAA: each Slave drives 48-bit PID + BCR + DCR Open-Drain MSb-first; lowest concatenated value wins; winner gets the Master-driven 7-bit DA + parity.

handshake_pairs.name: MASTER_CLOCK_STALL
handshake_pairs.rule: Master holds SCL LOW under conditions in Table 11 to slow down a transaction (ACK/NACK Phase, Write Parity, T-Bit transitions, DAA first bit).

dependency_graph.common_rule: Master drives SCL; Slaves sample SDA on rising SCL. Data on SDA must be stable while SCL HIGH; only S / P / Sr violate this rule.
dependency_graph.data_dependency: Master-Write byte N → T-Bit (parity) on SCL pulse 9 → Master-Write byte N+1. Slave-Read byte N → Slave T-Bit (1 continue / 0 end) → Slave-Read byte N+1 if T=1 and Master did not abort.
dependency_graph.no_scl_stretch: Slaves cannot delay the bus via SCL; only Master Clock Stall (Table 11) is allowed.

ordering_rules.multi_byte_ordering: Big-Endian over multi-byte fields (e.g. 48-bit Provisional ID streamed bit [47] first).
ordering_rules.byte_count: Number of bytes per transfer is unrestricted (limited by Master STOP + SETMWL/SETMRL).
ordering_rules.t_bit_per_word: Every SDR Data Word is followed by exactly one T-Bit on the 9th SCL pulse.
